fixes.row: How faith comes, is doubted and is measured: hearing, the word, "little faith", "great faith"
fixes.why: 'How faith comes' answers a question Christian traditions part on (faith as the gift of God, faith as a response to the heard word, the two together) and fills the answer with one side of it: 'faith comes by hearing' (Rom 10:17). The verses that speak of faith as given (Eph 2:8 'the gift of God', Rom 12:3 'the measure of faith God has given', Acts 3:16 'the faith that comes through Him') are filed in other rows under other labels, so a reader who looks here for 'how faith comes' is shown only the hearing account. The label says more than its verses do, and more than the hub as a whole does.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'Faith with hearing, the word, doubt, and "little" and "great" faith' (or 'Hearing, doubt and the measure of faith'), a plain list with no 'how'. Optionally add a one-line no-side note: 'Where the text speaks of faith as heard, as given (Rom 12:3, Eph 2:8) or as granted (Phil 1:29), see the other rows; the page does not say which comes first.'

fixes.row: Believe, and be baptized, repent, receive the Spirit
fixes.why: Yes, a single row of verbs in this form reads as a sequence. 'Believe, and be baptized, repent, receive the Spirit' is an imperative chain: it puts believing first, baptism second, repentance third and the Spirit last. That order is Mark 16:16's order (which is in the longer ending) and it is the reverse of Mark 1:15 ('Repent and believe') and Matt 21:32, where repentance comes before or with believing, and of Acts 2:38 order readers will bring to it (repent, be baptized, receive the Spirit). Whether baptism follows faith, whether the Spirit follows both or comes with believing (Acts 19:2, Eph 1:13) are exactly the points the note says the page takes no side on, and the label takes one by its grammar. Leading with Mark 16:16 (a verse the same note says the earliest manuscripts lack) and Acts 19:2 (the Berean's 'when you became believers' is one of two readings of the Greek participle, 'when' or 'since') adds to it.
fixes.fix: Relabel to match the noun row and the verb row above it: 'Believing with baptism, repentance and the Spirit'. Reorder the four leads to Acts 8:12, Mark 1:15, Eph 1:13, Mark 16:16 (so the first is not the doubtful ending, and repentance and the Spirit-sealing stand beside baptism). Keep the existing no-side note and the Mark 16:16 longer-ending note.

fixes.row: Faith with baptism, repentance and the Spirit
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Two things, both small. (1) Gal 5:22 is one of the four verses the hub itself says reads 'faithfulness' (the Spirit's fruit), yet it stands here under a row headed 'Faith', which contradicts the first noun row's note ('in the rest of this list it is faith'). A reader sees 'faithfulness' under a 'faith' label. (2) Of 14 verses only two name baptism and two repentance, but the lead examples are baptism, baptism, repentance, Spirit, with baptism named first in the label; ten of the fourteen verses are about the Spirit. The label order baptism-repentance-Spirit and the lead order are a weak sequence and over-weight the thinnest part of the row.
fixes.fix: Remove Gal 5:22 from this row (it stays in 'Where the gloss for πίστις is faithfulness') or add 'Gal 5:22 reads "faithfulness"' to the note. Relabel to 'Faith with repentance, baptism and the Spirit' (repentance first, the common order in Mark 1:15, Acts 20:21, Heb 6:1) and lead with Gal 3:2, Acts 20:21, Col 2:12, Eph 4:5.

fixes.row: Faith with being saved, made well or forgiven, and with grace
fixes.why: The two notes are joined without trouble and the row reads as no side, with one exception: the note names Eph 2:8 'which 2:9 follows with "not by works"', quoting only the half of the passage that bears on one side. Eph 2:10 ('created in Christ Jesus for good works') is the other half of the same sentence, and the row's own fourth lead, Jas 2:14 ('Can such faith save him?'), is not named. The note therefore tilts slightly toward grace-without-works, in a row about how grace, faith and works stand.
fixes.fix: Change the parenthesis to: '(Eph 2:8-10, where 2:9 reads "not by works" and 2:10 "created in Christ Jesus for good works"; Rom 4:16; Jas 2:14)'.

readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: The no-choice note is fair in what it says, but the row shows only one of the two readings. All four lead examples (Gal 2:16, Rom 3:22, Gal 3:22, Phil 3:9) are the Greek genitive constructions (literally 'faith of Jesus Christ') that the Berean renders 'faith in'; the same holds for Rom 3:26, Gal 2:20 and Jas 2:1. A reader sees 'faith in Jesus Christ' four times and 'faith of' once, in Rev 14:12 far down the list, and cannot tell that the 'in' is the Berean's choice of reading where the Greek has none (Col 1:4 and 2:5, by contrast, do use a preposition meaning 'in'). The note says 'forms the Berean reads "faith in" and "faith of"' but not which. That is the fact the 'faithfulness of Christ' reading rests on, and its absence makes the page look to prefer 'in'. Eph 3:17 ('that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith') is neither 'faith in' nor 'faith of' Christ; it is filed here only because the name stands in the verse.
fixes.fix: Extend the note: 'In Rom 3:22, 3:26, Gal 2:16, 2:20, 3:22, Phil 3:9 and Jas 2:1 the Greek has the name in the genitive ("faith of Jesus Christ"); the Berean's "faith in" there is its reading of the phrase. Elsewhere (Col 1:4, 2:5, Eph 1:15) the Greek has a preposition meaning "in". Readers part on the first group; the page does not choose.' Put Rev 14:12 among the four leads in place of Phil 3:9 or Gal 3:22. Move Eph 3:17 out of the row (it stays in the 'through faith' row) or add 'or Christ dwelling through faith' to the note.

readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Filing is right: Hab 2:4 is under the Hebrew word and not under belief or under the Pauline rows, and the label keeps 'faithfulness'. But the framing is New Testament first. (1) The row is last of thirteen in the noun form, after twelve Greek rows, so the Hebrew word that stands behind Paul's quotation is met last. (2) Its first example is Hab 2:4, the one verse of 43 where the Berean reads 'faith' rather than the label's 'faithfulness' (so the lead does not show the label, rule 6), and the very next sentence of the note introduces it by its New Testament quotations (Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11, Heb 10:38). A reader hears the Hebrew noun as a prelude to Paul. The Hebrew's own voice is the Psalms and Deuteronomy: the LORD's faithfulness (Ps 36:5, 89:1, Lam 3:23, Deut 32:4) and the faithful man (Prov 28:20).
fixes.fix: Lead with Ps 36:5, Lam 3:23, Deut 32:4, Ps 89:1 and keep Hab 2:4 inside the row (it is already there). Reword the note to say first what the Hebrew word is in the Psalms and Deuteronomy, then 'in Hab 2:4 the Berean reads it "faith"; the verse is quoted at Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11 and Heb 10:38'. If the builder can order rows, put this row first in the noun form, or at least before 'The faith'.

readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Isa 28:16 is the only Old Testament verse in this row and it does not belong under this label. The Berean reads 'the one who believes will never be shaken' (the Hebrew verb stands without an object), so the verse shows neither 'in Him' nor 'the One' nor 'the Lord': it fails rule 6. It is also an Old Testament verse filed under a heading that exists because of New Testament phrases (Rom 9:33 and 1 Pet 2:6 quote it and add 'in Him'). Putting it here lets the quotation's object stand as if it were Isaiah's.
fixes.fix: Move Isa 28:16 to 'Those who believe: "believers"' (the verb has no object, which is what that row is for) or leave it under More. Keep Rom 9:33 and 1 Pet 2:6 in this row.

readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Rule 3 is kept (nothing is attributed by rule, and the no-choice note is the right device), but the note is not true of every verse in the row. 'The text says only "Him", "the One" or "the Lord"' is not what Rom 4:24 ('Him who raised Jesus our Lord'), John 5:24 ('Him who sent Me') or John 6:29 ('the One He has sent') say: those are descriptions that the verse itself supplies, and no reader takes Rom 4:24 of Christ. The hub's own spec explains this; the reader cannot see it. A reader who checks the note against the verse finds it overstated.
fixes.fix: Reword the note: 'The text says "Him", "the One", "the Lord" or describes him ("Him who sent Me", "Him who raised Jesus"); where the verse does not name the person, the page does not choose.' Do not move Rom 4:24 or John 5:24 into the God row without Doug's per-record decision.

fixes.row: "The Lord is faithful", "He is faithful", "Faithful and True", the faithful witness
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: The note says 'readers take these of the Father or of Christ' and 'Rev 1:5 is the only one that names Jesus Christ'. For Heb 2:17 and 3:2 that is not so: 'a merciful and faithful high priest' and 'He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was' are about Jesus by the book's own words (Heb 2:9, 3:1) and nobody in the traditions reads them of the Father. Heb 11:11 ('considered Him faithful who had promised') is God, as in 'God is faithful'. Putting a settled attribution and an open one under one 'the page does not choose' makes the settled ones look contested.
fixes.fix: Extend the note: 'Heb 2:17 and 3:2 speak of the high priest whom Heb 3:1 calls Jesus; Heb 11:11 of the one who had promised. The rest say "the Lord", "He", or "the One who calls you" and readers take them of the Father or of Christ; the page does not choose.'

fixes.row: More (adjective): faithful servants, stewards, brothers, saints; "Trustworthy is the saying"
fixes.why: Yes, losing them misrepresents the adjective. Under the title 'Called faithful, called believing' the three rows show God or the Lord as faithful, and believers as 'believing'. Of 67 verses, 41 (61%) are under unlabelled More, and the largest part of that is the commonest use in the Gospels and the Epistles: a person who is faithful, the 'good and faithful servant', the faithful steward (1 Cor 4:2), Moses faithful in God's house (Heb 3:5), 'be faithful unto death' (Rev 2:10), Antipas 'my faithful witness'. That is human faithfulness as steadfast service, which the Hebrew side of the hub (אמן, 'faithful') also carries and which a rabbi will look for. The result presents the Greek πιστός as God's attribute plus a gloss for 'believers' only (rule 4: one sense presented as the whole). 'Trustworthy is the saying' is the Pastoral formula (1 Tim 1:15, 3:1, 4:9, 2 Tim 2:11, Titus 3:8) and is the same adjective; it is a reasoned loss only if the page says so. The builder's own report says restoring either is a one-row job.
fixes.fix: Restore two labelled rows from More: 'Faithful servants, stewards, brothers, ministers and witnesses' (about 27 verses: Matt 24:45, 25:21, 25:23, Luke 12:42, 16:10-12, 19:17, 1 Cor 4:2, 4:17, Eph 6:21, Col 1:7, 4:7, 4:9, 1 Pet 5:12, Heb 3:5, Rev 2:10, 2:13, 17:14, 3 John 5, 2 Tim 2:2 and the like) with the same gloss-not-Greek note as the 'believing' row; and '"Trustworthy is the saying"' (1 Tim 1:15, 3:1, 4:9, 2 Tim 2:11, Titus 1:9, 3:8, Rev 21:5, 22:6). Leave 'of little faith' in More (the noun row 'little faith' already shows it).

fixes.row: Where the gloss for πίστις is "faithfulness", not "faith"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Fair to both readings: the page lets the gloss decide, does not say faith and faithfulness are one meaning and does not say which a 'faith' verse carries; that is the right stance for the verdict flagged high. Two small misses. The fourth lead, Titus 2:10, is in the Berean's English 'good faith', so it does not show the label's word (rule 6), though the note names 'fidelity'. And Matt 23:23, the one Gospel verse that sets 'the law' beside this word (law: justice, mercy, faithfulness), is kept out of the law row by design, so a rabbi looking at 'Faith and the law' will not meet it.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: 'Titus 2:10 reads "good faith" in the Berean.' Add one line to the law row's note, 'Matt 23:23 (the law: justice, mercy and faithfulness) is under "faithfulness", where the gloss puts it'.

worker_points.point: 1. Belief or faithfulness: noun 1 on MACULA's gloss; the same split for the Hebrew noun, the Hebrew verb and the adjective; the noun, verb and adjective never said to be one thing.
worker_points.why: Sound and fair to both readings; the note does not say which meaning a 'faith' verse carries, which is the right restraint. Hab 2:4 is filed under the Hebrew word 'faithfulness' (row 13), not under belief and not under the Pauline rows, which is correct for the rabbi seat: אֱמוּנָה is faithfulness in Hebrew and the hub says so. Needed: reorder the Hebrew row's leads and note so the verse is not introduced by its New Testament quotations; lead the Greek gloss row with something that shows the word (Titus 2:10); keep Gal 5:22 out of the 'Spirit' faith row. See fixes.

worker_points.point: 2. Faith in Christ or Christ's faithfulness: noun 3, 23 verses, hand pick, note: the page does not choose.
worker_points.why: The no-choice note is right but all four leads show only the Berean's 'faith in' where the Greek is a genitive, and the note does not tell the reader which verses those are. Fair to both readings only after the note names them and a 'faith of Jesus' lead (Rev 14:12) is among the four. Eph 3:17 is not a 'faith in/of' phrase and should leave the row.

worker_points.point: 3. Faith and works side by side: noun 5, 6, 7 with match all (Jas 2:24, Rom 3:28, Gal 2:16 in every row they fit); verb 8 joins works with credited, justified under a no-side note; noun 6 joins the law with circumcision; noun 7 carries Rom 4:5, 4:9, 4:11.
worker_points.why: Checked row by row. Jas 2:24 and Rom 3:28 stand together in rows 2, 5 and 7, Gal 2:16 in 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7. Leads in 'Faith and works' are James, Paul, James, Paul; in the law row Gal 3:24, Rom 3:30, Rom 3:31 ('we uphold the law'), Rev 14:12 (the commandments), which is evenly spread; in the 'righteousness, justified, credited' row three Pauline leads and Jas 2:24 fourth, which is what the text holds under those words and is not a tilt because 'a verse that names works as well stands in the row for works' is in the note. Labels use the text's words (credited, justified, works). The verb row's leads (John 6:29, Titus 3:8, Gen 15:6, Acts 13:39) are balanced. No fix. Optional: Wesleyan and Catholic readers might prefer Gal 2:16 or Jas 2:24 swapped up in row 7.

worker_points.point: 4. Baptism, repentance and the Spirit merged into one row per form under one no-side note (Mark 16:16 longer ending, Acts 2:38, Acts 8:12-13, 19:4, Col 2:12, Eph 4:5): does the single row read as a sequence?
worker_points.why: The noun row ('Faith with ...', a list under 'with') does not read as a sequence much, though the label order and lead order are baptism first and should lead with repentance as the common order; the verb row ('Believe, and be baptized, repent, receive the Spirit') does read as a sequence, believing then baptism then repentance then the Spirit, which is Mark 16:16's order and the reverse of Mark 1:15. Relabel it as a 'with' list. Acts 2:38 contains no faith word and so cannot be in this hub; see 'missing'.
The two notes read cleanly as one no-side note. The grace sentence cites Eph 2:9 ('not by works') without 2:10 or Jas 2:14 and so leans one way. Fix is a one-clause change to the parenthesis.

worker_points.point: 6. Eternal life: Acts 13:48 in verb row 6 on purpose with every believing-and-life verse; the label does not imply direction.
worker_points.why: 'With' is a neutral connector and the verse is among all the others that put believing and life in one verse; the reader is not told what 'appointed' means. The no-side stance on election is kept.

worker_points.point: 7. Repentance is two verses in noun 9 and two in verb 7, inside the baptism rows; flagged high on its own hub.
worker_points.why: Four verses is thin but not misleading: the label names it and the note covers it. The repentance hub will carry the load. No fix beyond the reorder in the baptism fixes (repentance named first).

worker_points.point: 8. 'The faith' (noun 12): note that readers part on whether it means what is believed or the believing.
worker_points.why: The note states the parting evenly (what is believed, or the believing itself) and the four leads (kept, contended for, abandoned, stand firm in) are the text's own verbs. Catholic and Orthodox readers can accept 'what is believed'; Baptist and Reformed 'the believing' or both. No fix.

worker_points.point: 9. Divine persons by hand: noun 3 and 4, verb 1 and 2, adjective 1; unnamed (verb 3, adjective 2) with no-choice notes; John 14:1 in two rows; read verb 3 (John 5:24, 5:38, 6:29 descriptions, Matt 27:42 the crowd).
worker_points.why: The persons are placed only by hand and John 14:1 in two rows is the right way to show a verse that names both. The two no-choice notes are not true of every verse in their rows (verb 3: descriptions like 'Him who raised Jesus'; adjective 2: Heb 2:17, 3:2 speak of Jesus by the book's own context, and Heb 11:11 of God). Matt 27:42 (the crowd's taunt, 'we will believe in Him') is in the row because it says 'believe in Him'; it stands fine, since the verse itself says what is claimed, but is the one verse in the row spoken by non-believers. Isa 28:16 should leave verb 3. See fixes.

worker_points.point: 10. Verses whose English does not show the Hebrew/Greek stay under More: Job 15:22, Isa 55:3, Ps 27:13; 1 Tim 2:7.
worker_points.why: Right call under rule 6; the Berean's English ('despairs of his return', 'My loving devotion promised to David') does not show the label's word, so they are better under More than under a label they do not display.

worker_points.point: 11. What the merging hid: faithful servants, stewards, brothers, ministers, saints (27) and 'Trustworthy is the saying' (8) now under More with no label; 'Believing, trusting a person' now inside verb 4.
worker_points.why: Yes, restore both adjective rows: 41 of 67 adjective verses unlabelled hides the commonest sense of the word (a faithful person), which gives the form a false profile (God faithful, believers 'believing'). The loss in verb 4 is not a misrepresentation: Gen 45:26, Judg 11:20, 1 Sam 27:12 and Mic 7:5 are among the four leads or the row's contents, and the ordinary human use of the verb stays visible.

missing.what: Two faith-word verses are in no row and not even under More: Deut 32:20 (the Hebrew אֱמֻן, 'children of unfaithfulness' in the Berean; it is the only other use of the noun h529 besides Deut 32:4, which is in the Hebrew row) and Titus 1:4 ('our common faith', πίστις). The worker lists both as clause-filing and 'unfaithfulness' regex misses. Neither is misleading alone, but a hub that claims to hold the word's uses should hold them.

Faith beside baptism in the next verse is named only in a note (noun row 9 for Gal 3:26-27; the verb row's _why for Acts 16:31-33) and shown nowhere. The note is honest, but the verb row's note does not mention Acts 16:31-33 at all, so a Baptist, Lutheran or Catholic reader looking for the strongest narrative pairing finds nothing. Add a sentence to the verb baptism row's note naming Acts 16:31-33, as the noun row does for Gal 3:26-27.

summary: The hub is sound on the hard points: the gloss split, the works/law/justified rows side by side, the divine persons by hand and Gen 15:6 leading its row are all fair, and Hab 2:4 is filed under the Hebrew word and not under belief. It should ship after relabelling the verb baptism row (it reads as a sequence) and 'How faith comes' (it answers a contested question with one side), softening the Eph 2:8-9 note, naming the Greek genitives in the faith-in-Christ note, moving Isa 28:16 out of the 'Him' row, putting the Hebrew faithfulness row's own voice before its New Testament quotations, and restoring the faithful-servants and trustworthy-saying rows.
